name: Observation of a new boson at a mass of 125 GeV
notes: The collaboration wording is "observation of a new boson", not "discovery of the Higgs boson".

significance.quote: a local significance of 5.0 standard deviations

summary.plain: CMS reported an excess of events above background near 125 GeV that, in its words, signals the production of a new particle, at a joint CERN seminar on 4 July 2012. The paper gives a mass of 125.3 ± 0.4 (stat) ± 0.5 (syst) GeV and says the two-photon decay indicates a boson with spin different from one.
summary.technical: Search for the standard model Higgs boson in five decay modes (γγ, ZZ, WW, ττ, bb̄) with up to 5.1 fb⁻¹ at 7 TeV and 5.3 fb⁻¹ at 8 TeV: an excess with local significance 5.0 standard deviations at a mass near 125 GeV (5.8 expected for a standard model Higgs boson of that mass); a fit to the γγ and ZZ signals gives 125.3 ± 0.4 (stat) ± 0.5 (syst) GeV; the diphoton decay indicates a boson with spin different from one.

title: Observation of a new boson at a mass of 125 GeV with the CMS experiment at the LHC
why_it_matters: The paper's introduction says the question of how the W and Z gauge bosons acquire mass whilst the photon remains massless is still open; introducing a complex scalar doublet field leads to the generation of the W and Z masses and to the prediction of the standard model Higgs boson, and the scalar field also gives mass to the fundamental fermions through the Yukawa interaction. CMS reports an excess that signals the production of a new particle near 125 GeV.
